To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

compressive sampling (CS) is a novel sensing/sensing paradigm that goes against common wisdom in data sampling and that it asserts that one can reconstruct certain signals and images using far fewer samples or observations than traditional methods use.
compressive sampling is a new sampling paradigm that can achieve the same reconstruction quality as Shannon's sampling theorem, but with a far lower number of samples.
the compressive sampling method is an effective and accurate method for sampling and reconstructing signals.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new algorithms and architectures for signal and image processing based on the principles of compressive sampling.
the design and implementation of efficient algorithms for compressive sampling and recovery, as well as with the development of novel sampling devices that implement the CS paradigm.

compressive sensing can be applied in any field where the sampling is done by a linear transformation.
the compressive sampling theory is a new theory of signal acquisition and processing that allows one to recover certain signals and image from a small set of linear projections of those signals.
the theory of compressible signals and compressive sampling is a major breakthrough in signal processing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CS is a new sampling paradigm that is based on the idea of sparse representations.
the CS theory provides a new paradigm for sampling, and the CS algorithm provides an efficient way of solving the underdetermined linear system.
we have developed a new sampling paradigm for data acquisition.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the number of measurements needed to recover a signal or image is proportional to the sparsity of the signal or image.
the theory of CS is not just another sampling theory, but rather a completely new way to acquire and represent signals, images and other structured data.
CS theory is indeed a valid and useful paradigm in the real world.
